concepts.learning_objective: Interpret dy/dx as the rate of change of y with respect to x and evaluate it at a given point.
Use the chain rule to relate rates of change of quantities that vary with time.
Find marginal cost and marginal revenue as derivatives of total cost and total revenue.
State the definitions of increasing, decreasing, strictly increasing and strictly decreasing functions on an interval.
Use the sign of f′(x) on an interval to decide whether f is strictly increasing, strictly decreasing or constant.
Find the intervals in which a function is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing using its critical points.

topics.title: Maximum and minimum values and critical points

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the maximum, minimum and extreme values of a function on an interval.
Find the critical points of a function and recognise that f′(c) = 0 is necessary but not sufficient for a local extremum.
Classify a critical point using the change in sign of f′(x) as x increases through it.
Classify a critical point using the sign of f″(c) and recognise when the test fails.

topics.title: Absolute maximum and minimum on a closed interval

concepts.learning_objective: State that a continuous function on a closed interval attains an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum.
Find absolute maximum and minimum values by comparing f at the critical points and the end points.

topics.title: Applied problems on maxima and minima

concepts.learning_objective: Model number and mensuration situations as functions and find their maximum or minimum values.
Solve real-life optimisation problems such as maximum volume and maximum revenue.
